name: multi_event_update_of
comment: Several events in one declaration with an UPDATE OF narrowing: SQLite has single-event triggers, so it renders one per event named <name>_<event> (the narrowing only on the update one) and drops every possible per-event name; SQL Server lists the events and emulates the narrowing with an if not (update(...)) return; prologue; PostgreSQL joins the events with or and narrows natively. {old: cols} is deleted on SQL Server.

trigger.name: trg_widgets_changes
trigger.sql: insert into widget_log (widget_id, at) select o.id, {now} from {old: id} o;

create:
create trigger trg_widgets_changes_update after update of name, price on widgets for each row
begin
insert into widget_log (widget_id, at) select o.id, strftime('%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%fZ', 'now') from (select old.id as id) o;
end

create trigger trg_widgets_changes_delete after delete on widgets for each row
begin
insert into widget_log (widget_id, at) select o.id, strftime('%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%fZ', 'now') from (select old.id as id) o;
end

drop: if object_id(N'trg_widgets_changes', N'TR') is not null drop trigger [trg_widgets_changes]

create: create trigger "trg_widgets_changes" after update of "name", "price" or delete on "widgets" for each row execute function "trg_widgets_changes_fn"()
